exposure: Siblings born to the same mother who experienced different types of births (vaginal and cesarean)
outcome: Delayed initiation of breastfeeding (not being breastfed in the first 24 hours)
cohort: Mothers and infants in the state of Odisha in eastern India between 2007 and 2011
finding: Babies born by cesarean in Odisha are about 11 percentage points more likely to experience delayed initiation of breastfeeding compared with babies born vaginally, after controlling for many potential confounders using mother fixed effects.
mod_finding: Babies born by cesarean in Odisha are about 11 percentage points more likely to experience delayed initiation of breastfeeding compared with babies born vaginally.
